seoTitle: Saint Maroun Storybook for Children | The Hermit on the Hill
seoDescription: Saint Maroun storybook for ages 6-12: ten illustrated pages about a hermit on a Syrian hilltop, the people who climbed up to meet him, and the Maronite family that took his name, with a family reflection.
h1: Saint Maroun: The Hermit on the Hill
intro: Climb a Syrian hill, meet the hermit who prayed under the open sky, and see how a whole family of faith grew from one quiet life. Read together, then listen.
shortAnswer: This ten-page Saint Maroun storybook for ages 6 to 12 follows a hermit of the late 300s from his hilltop near Cyrrhus to the Maronite family that carries his name. It ends with a narrated family reflection to share together.
summaryHtml:
Saint Maroun lived in the open air on a hilltop in northern Syria. People climbed up to meet him, and his way of prayer spread. Nine narrative pages end with a narrated family reflection.

What This Story Covers

  • A Hilltop Under the Sky
  • A Day Made of Prayer
  • People Begin to Climb the Hill
  • Teaching Without a Classroom
  • Friends Who Joined Him
  • A Letter from Far Away
  • A Short Illness
  • Villages Who Wanted Him Near
  • A Name That Became a Family
familyReadingHtml:
With a parent or caregiver, read Psalm 92:13. Talk about what it means to flourish like a palm tree or a cedar of Lebanon.

The final page offers a question, a Bible reading, a small action and a short prayer. A trusted adult can read it aloud and stop to talk about any part.
aboutHtml: Illustrations are imaginative composites, not portraits or eyewitness scenes. Maroun's life is known mostly from one chapter by Theodoret of Cyrrhus, who never met him, so the story leaves out his childhood and family because nobody knows them. The letter from John Chrysostom is addressed to a monk named Maron, and many people believe he meant this Maroun. The Maronite Church traces its name to him, though its early history is still debated by historians.

faq.a: A hermit of the late 300s who lived on a hilltop near Cyrrhus in northern Syria. The Maronite Church is named after him. His feast is on 9 February.
It follows the bishop Theodoret's chapter about Maroun, the one close account of his life. Where the sources are silent, the story says so and invents nothing.
Children ages 6 to 12, reading or listening with family. Ten illustrated pages end with a four-part family reflection.
